description: A theme's manifest.json: what the theme is, which of its layers it has and what each app may load from it. A theme is a folder (its host's themes/<name>/), or that folder zipped as one file (<name>.baudetheme) to pass round. A folder with no manifest (theme.css, tokens.json) is a theme of kind colours or skin, as its files say.

name.description: Its name, its folder's: 1 to 40 letters, digits, spaces, - or _.

kind.description: Its highest layer: colours (tokens.json: every app's colours), skin (colours, and the desktop apps' look over theirs: theme.css, a GTK theme), scene (a skin, and a space Baude's things are placed in: scene.json). Each layer has the ones under it, which the widgets put in a scene are drawn with.

description.description: One line saying what it is, for Settings → Theme and Meta.

tokens.description: Whether it has tokens.json (ThemeFiles' tokens): colours over schema/tokens', light and dark, for every app.

skin.description: Its skin, the desktop apps': left out for none.

scene.description: Its scene: left out for none.

assets.description: Each file a scene or a skin uses, by its path in the folder: models/ (.obj, .glb), textures/ (.png, .jpg, .webp, .hdr), fonts/ (.ttf, .otf), shaders/ (.glsl, the desktop's). Every app may read them; none is run.

credits.description: Where the theme's files that someone else made come from, and under what licence: left out for none.
